clue.text: Riding with us

definitions.meaning: travelling aboard a vehicle, ship or plane
part of our team, having joined the group

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both aboard a vehicle as a passenger and, idiomatically, signed up as a member of a team.

clue.text: Brief operation on model's face

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: OP is a short form of operation
a model's work is to pose

explanation.surface: A quick cosmetic procedure on a fashion model's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' looks like the part being operated on; it is the verb meaning to confront. 'on' stacks OP above POSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To face an opponent is to stand against or oppose them.

clue.text: Dog in front of building, something well worth having

indicators.note: front of takes only the first letter of building

parts.note: an asset is a valuable thing

explanation.surface: A dog sitting outside a building, which is a real prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' gives B, from 'building'. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged hound with long ears is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Always a great name for a newspaper?

parts.note: great in the sense of big and high, tall
The Times is a famous newspaper title, the question mark marking an example

explanation.surface: Musing on a grand title for a daily paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as A TALL TIMES, a great Times, i.e. a big edition of the London newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means on every occasion, without exception, just as always does.

clue.text: Round after silent film

indicators.note: after places the round letter behind the word for silent

parts.note: dumb means silent
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A round of drinks after seeing a silent movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts O after DUMB. 'Silent film' looks like one phrase, but the two words are split up.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the 1941 Disney animated feature about a flying baby elephant.

clue.text: Rages at new riot control measure

indicators.note: new suggests these letters take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone furious at a newly introduced crowd-control policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the seven letters of RAGES AT.
explanation.definitionFit: This irritant spray is a standard tool police use to disperse rioting crowds.

clue.text: Sailor, ahead of a giddy aunt, carrying large spider

indicators.note: ahead of puts the sailor first in the order

parts.note: a tar is an old term for a sailor

indicators.note: carrying means the jumbled aunt holds the letter for large inside it
giddy means the letters of aunt are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor in front of a dizzy aunt who is holding a huge spider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giddy' rearranges AUNT into NTUA; 'carrying' puts L inside it to give NTULA.
explanation.definitionFit: A big hairy arachnid, often kept as a pet, is this kind of spider.

clue.text: Fit in extra guest

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words extra guest

explanation.surface: Squeezing in one more guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like a verb about squeezing someone in; it is a noun, a bout of shivering.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a malarial fever, or a fit of shivering.

clue.text: Get heard abroad, and understood

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Making yourself heard overseas and being understood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges the letters of GET HEARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To have gathered something is to have inferred or understood it.

clue.text: Mata Hari, perhaps — young woman smuggling good telescope

indicators.note: smuggling means the letter for good is slipped inside the pair

parts.note: Mata Hari was a famous spy, an example
a lass is a young woman

explanation.surface: A female spy sneaking a fine telescope through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smuggling' puts G between the two joined pieces, so the spy and the girl hide the letter between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hand-held telescope is called this.

clue.text: Finished last of lasagna, food of Italian origin

parts.note: something finished is past, over and done

indicators.note: last of tells us to take only the final letter of lasagna

explanation.surface: Someone polishing off the remains of a lasagne, an Italian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' takes the A ending 'lasagna'. The lasagna in the surface is itself an example of the answer, which helps the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti, macaroni and the like are a staple foodstuff that originated in Italy.

clue.text: Inlaid work — make sample

parts.note: a make of car is a marque, a brand
to sample is to try

explanation.surface: An instruction to produce a specimen piece of decorative inlay.
explanation.definitionFit: This craft is decorative inlay of shaped veneers of wood set into furniture surfaces.

clue.text: Certain, after short time, to become fascinated

indicators.note: after places the word for certain following the short period

parts.note: a spell is a brief period
certain, as in sure to happen, is bound

explanation.surface: Someone who is sure to be enthralled after only a little while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' sets the word for certain behind the short period; 'certain' is meant in the sense of 'bound to win'. 'to become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held as if by magic is utterly fascinated, rapt and entranced.

clue.text: Fine jet

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to spurt or gush up, as liquid does

explanation.definitionFit: The word means in good health, and as a verb it means to spring or surge up as a fountain does.

clue.text: Be taken round new training ship

indicators.note: taken round means the letters of Be enclose the next part
new says the letters of training are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being shown around a fresh training vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the eight letters of 'training', and 'taken round' wraps the two letters of 'Be' about the result.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a two-masted sailing vessel, a type of ship.

clue.text: Concealed around new accommodation in rear

indicators.note: around means the word for concealed goes about the letter for new

parts.note: concealed means hid
quarters are lodgings or accommodation

explanation.surface: Something hidden near freshly built lodgings at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts N inside the word for concealed, making HIND. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The back legs and rump of an animal, its rear end, are called by this word.

clue.text: Dixon's London manor shown in clip incompletely prepared

parts.note: to clip is to dock, cut short
green means immature or not ready

explanation.surface: A London police patch featured in a hastily made film clip.
explanation.walkthrough: Dixon of Dock Green was a long-running British TV police series; 'manor' is police slang for a beat. 'shown in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: PC George Dixon policed this fictional East London district in the BBC series.

clue.text: Boiled tripe provided after a preprandial drink

indicators.note: after places the jumbled tripe and the condition behind the letter A
boiled suggests the letters of tripe are stirred up

parts.note: provided means if

explanation.surface: Cooked offal served after a pre-dinner drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boiled' rearranges the five letters of 'tripe' into PERIT. 'Preprandial' means before a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite is this.

clue.text: False story about king results in conflict

indicators.note: about means the story is wrapped around the letter for king

parts.note: fiction is an invented story
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A fabricated tale about a monarch leads to war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside FICTION. 'results in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Disagreement and clashing between people is called this, by extension of rubbing.

clue.text: Method used to buy some — brief argument follows

indicators.note: follows puts the argument word after the word for some

parts.note: some, a portion, is part
an exchange is a short heated row

explanation.surface: A buying technique, followed by a brief dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' puts the argument after the word for some. 'Brief argument' fits because a sharp exchange of words is a short quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying for a new car partly by handing over your old one is a common way of buying.

clue.text: Engineers' former tax break

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
a cess was an old tax or levy

explanation.surface: Engineers enjoying a tax holiday from years ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause in proceedings, such as Parliament's holiday, is a break.

clue.text: Sportsman in corner close to boxer

parts.note: an angle is a corner

indicators.note: close to takes the final letter of boxer

explanation.surface: A sportsman in a boxing-ring corner, near the boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corner' and 'boxer' suggest boxing; the sportsman is a fisherman. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fishes with rod and line is a kind of sportsman.

clue.text: Runs excellent competition

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: Someone who runs a first-rate contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest of speed between runners or vehicles is a kind of competition.

clue.text: Get on outfit for old charity

parts.note: to get on is to grow older, to age
an outfit is a business or firm, a concern

explanation.surface: An instruction to dress up for a charity event of years gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: AGE CONCERN was a British charity for older people, since merged into Age UK, hence 'old'. 'Outfit' is a business, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a British charity that supported elderly people before merging into a successor body.

clue.text: Faith shown by Indian leader in Delhi

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

indicators.note: leader in takes the first letter of Delhi

explanation.surface: Religious belief displayed by an Indian politician in Delhi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like India but means a North American people, the CREE. 'shown by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of religious beliefs, a faith.

clue.text: Part of church making error dropping Latin

indicators.note: dropping says the letter for Latin is removed

parts.note: to lapse is to slip or make an error

explanation.surface: A section of a church where someone slipped up by leaving out the Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes L from LAPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church is this.

clue.text: Epilogue in story reportedly by King?

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is spoken and we write what is heard

parts.note: a story is a tale
the king is a chess piece, the question mark flagging an example

explanation.surface: An epilogue in a novel supposedly by Stephen King.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' suggests the novelist; it is a chess piece. TALE heard aloud gives TAIL; 'by' joins the two parts and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A closing section added to the end of a book or piece of music is an epilogue.

clue.text: One portion is perfect

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a deal is an amount or share, as in a good deal

explanation.surface: A single serving is just right.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flawless, exactly as wished for, is perfect.

clue.text: Ballerina — often misspelt, Darcey's last name

indicators.note: misspelt says the letters of often are put in the wrong order
last takes only the final letter of Darcey's

explanation.surface: A note that a ballerina's surname is frequently spelt wrongly, as with Darcey Bussell's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misspelt' rearranges OFTEN into FONTE; 'last' takes Y from Darcey. Margot FONTEYN was a celebrated British prima ballerina.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Margot was a renowned English prima ballerina with the Royal Ballet.

clue.text: Actor's assistant, a help in the theatre

definitions.text: Actor's assistant, a help in the theatre

parts.words: Actor's assistant, a help in the theatre
parts.note: a backstage helper who looks after a performer's costumes and helps them change; the word also suggests kitchen furniture

explanation.definitionFit: In theatres, the person who helps an actor into costume between scenes has this job title.
